newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends firmer, c.bank seen capping rise.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends firmer, c.bank seen capping rise.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,560-1,565 per dollar, up from the morning's 1,575-1,580 but a touch softer from midday's highs of 1,555 as the central bank was seen capping the rise, dealers said.
"The central bank started bidding for dollars to halt a further lev rise after the lev advanced to 1,555-1,560 at midday due to higher foreign currency supply," a commercial bank dealer said.
The lev eased to 1,570 due to central bank dollar buying but quickly recovered to 1,560-1,565 after the central bank withdrew from the market in the afternoon.
Central bank officials were unavailable for comment.
"If the central bank was not buying dollars the lev could have firmed above 1,550 today," another dealer said.
Banks and clients have been paring foreign exchange positions in the past month to profit on high-yield lev-denominated investments as the lev has traded stable near 1,600.
The central bank main interest rate is now set at 17.14 percent monthly or 205.68 percent annually. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
